messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT DETECTED — smart-routing anomalies across EU regions. Elevated 5xxs and fallback churn. Paging on-call for incidents channel.
lia: on it, grabbing context. which customers affected?
andrew: seeing errors spike ~03:22 UTC in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1, 5xxs jump to ~5% request volume. latency 95p -> 1.8s from 400ms.
tess: RUM shows correlated client timeouts for AcmeCorp & BrightShop. hitting our route policy that prefers redwood-large then falls back to quantized.
kayla: logs look like rapid model variant switch: route tries redwood-large-eu, capacity hit, policy falls back to redwood-small-quant, then back to large when capacity freed -> loop.
lia: that sounds like the known fallback loop bug where fallback policy had no cooldown. are we seeing any force-* overrides?
deploy-bot: deploys: no deploys in last 15m.
andrew: we do have an active emergency override from the infra team earlier: `override_route --policy=aggressive-cost-savings --max_retries=0` applied 20m ago. not sure who applied.
lia: can someone post the exact override command from audit?
sre-ops-bot: audit log -> `2026-03-15T03:05:23Z: user=platform-ops action=force-route policy=aggressive-cost-savings region_preference=eu-west,eu-central`
tess: OK that aligns. policy is aggressive and will immediately fallback to cheaper variants when the preferred model hits load. without cooldown that causes oscillation.
kayla: impact: 5% error rate overall in EU, but specific customers (AcmeCorp) see up to 12% request failures and degraded quality.
lia: plan: 1) disable fallback policy (make routing strict) 2) pin critical customer routes to a stable variant 3) scale dedicated capacity in eu-west as temporary relief 4) coordinate on-call handoff to eng-runtime for fix. any objections?
andrew: disabling fallback might push more traffic to redwood-large; we need capacity increase first or we'll see wholesale failures. scaling now.
lia: executing temporary mitigation: `/infra override --set-routing=stable --reason="incident mitigation"`
deploy-bot: command executed by lia at 03:30 UTC: `--set-routing=stable` -> OK.
tess: immediately seeing less oscillation in router logs. fallback attempts drop by 80%.
kayla: but traffic now backs up on eu-west model pods, CPU spikes. 2 pods OOM, restarting.
lia: hmm. given that, I propose a controlled force-region to eu-central for a subset of sessions to rebalance. we can split by customer tag and move non-critical traffic.
andrew: be careful — we had a similar manual force-region last month that caused downstream cache invalidation and a cascade. make the change on a small % first.
lia: doing 10% reroute: `/infra route-split --from=eu-west --to=eu-central --pct=10 --tag=non-critical`
deploy-bot: route-split applied.
tess: metrics: 10% shifted, eu-central nodes absorb without issues. errors for AcmeCorp drop to 6%. overall errors 3.8%.
kayla: warning: hitting model variant mismatch in eu-central — it serves quantized model by default for cost-savings. requests that rely on large-model features see degraded outputs. logged QA complaints from BrightShop.
lia: we need to pin AcmeCorp to redwood-large in eu-central for the session slice. applying: `/infra force-model --region=eu-central --model=redwood-large --selector=customer:acmecorp`
andrew: wait — that force-model will bypass autoscaling triggers. if we pin too many sessions we might starve other customers. confirm limits.
lia: limit 50 instances, TTL 30m. applying now.
deploy-bot: `force-model` executed by lia at 03:41 UTC. TTL=30m, limit=50.
tess: immediate improvement for AcmeCorp. errors down to 1.5%. quality back to normal. :thumbsup:
kayla: but monitoring shows a spike in auth token churn and cache misses — pinned sessions weren't using cached KV state in eu-central, so backend had to recompute leading to increased DB load. DB CPU up 40%.
andrew: DB alarm firing. if DB gets saturated we cascade elsewhere. We should revert non-critical pins and scale DB read replicas.
lia: rolling back the 10% split first to reduce load and avoid full revert of pins. `/infra route-split --from=eu-central --to=eu-west --pct=10`
deploy-bot: route-split rollback executed.
tess: after rollback, eu-central DB load drops but eu-west still overloaded.
kayla: at 03:50 UTC eng-runtime reports that the TTL for the force-model expired but the forced pins were re-applied by a concurrent automation rule. looks like two rules clashed: the emergency policy enforcer re-pinned sessions expecting the other override to remain.
lia: oh no — so our manual override triggered an automation that reasserted pins, causing persistent load. we need to disable that automation. who owns it?
andrew: automation owner is eng-runtime. @eng-runtime can you pause the reassertion job?
eng-runtime: pausing job now. paused at 03:53 UTC.
lia: monitoring — pinned sessions count falling. DB metrics trending down.
nina (observability): quick note: we've captured the request traces for the loop window; saving to /observability/incidents/1771234567 for postmortem.
tess: customer comms: sending alert to impacted customers: AcmeCorp & BrightShop with initial impact and mitigation steps.
lia: final mitigation summary: disabled aggressive fallback policy, applied targeted route-split (reverted), pinned critical customer sessions to stable variant with TTL, paused automation reasserting pins, scaled temporary capacity, and engaged eng-runtime for bug fix.
andrew: side effects observed and logged: cache invalidations, DB load spike, automation race reapplying pins, and temporary increase in 95p latency for non-pin customers.
kayla: next steps: eng-runtime will add cooldown to fallback policy, add safety checks to force-model automation, and add autoscaler-aware pinning that increments capacity reservations.
eng-runtime: acknowledged. will take lead on postmortem and code fix. ETA initial patch 48h.
lia: on-call handoff — I'm wrapping up and handing to andrew for next shift. andrew take over?
andrew: taking over. I've set a reminder for follow-up, and scheduled a 1hr post-incident sync at 10:00 UTC.	lia: thanks all. adding incident severity P1 -> P2 after mitigation.
incident-bot: incident closed (mitigated) at 03:58 UTC. follow-up postmortem scheduled. :calendar:
